scope.boundary: Bounded static store and reader classification. No exhaustive alias analysis, actual callback binding, host implementation or runtime safety result.

Owns the separate allocation, fence and EndTiling reservation contracts.
Owns qualified worker event waits and conditional presentation order.

storeFamilies.claim: Reservation loops acquire the worker lock, can rewrite its old word on a failed comparison, and release it with zero.

fill255Boundary.question: Does the selected unaligned 255-byte fill retain the adjacent wrapper saves and return normally?
fill255Boundary.call: 0x826A7C10 calls 0x827F7BB0 with full r3=D=F+81, r4=0 and r5=255, returning to 0x826A7C14. Reuse the admitted zero-extended, nonwrapping wrapper frame S=F+352; ABI alignment supplies F mod4=0.
fill255Boundary.predicates: Require retained executable/LR state, valid ABI-aligned S>=352, nonwrapping address arithmetic, writable mapped [D,D+255), no interfering writer and no destructive physical alias with protected frame/caller bytes. This is the fixed call, not arbitrary sizes or full-SP contexts.
fill255Boundary.prefix: 0x827F7BB0/0x827F7BB4 initializes CTR=256 and 0x827F7BB8 copies D to r6. Alignment testing at 0x827F7BCC/0x827F7BD0 executes the 0x827F7BC4 byte store three times at F+81/F+82/F+83. r5 becomes 252 and r6 becomes F+84; the aligned fourth test exits with CTR=252.
fill255Boundary.groupsAndTail: 0x827F7BD8 selects 15 groups. Four scalar BE32 stores at 0x827F7BE8/0x827F7BEC/0x827F7BF0/0x827F7BF4 execute 15 times with a 16-byte step, covering [F+84,F+324). Three residual BE32 stores at 0x827F7C0C/0x827F7C18/0x827F7C24 cover F+324..F+335. At 0x827F7C2C, 252&3=0; CTR becomes zero and 0x827F7C34 returns through LR without a byte tail. Exactly 66 scalar stores write 255 distinct zero bytes in [F+81,F+336), with no vector or cacheline rounding.
fill255Boundary.returnEffects: Full r3 remains D; final r5=252, r6=F+336 and r0=r4=CTR=0. Only GPR r0/r4/r5/r6, CTR and CR0 are assigned. Final CR0 has EQ=1, LT=GT=0 and SO from unchanged XER.SO. Actual r1/SP, full r31, other GPRs, LR, floating/vector registers, XER and other CR fields remain unchanged. The leaf has no data read, stack access, outgoing call or explicit cache operation.
fill255Boundary.saveRetention: The fill excludes byte F+80, backchain [F,F+4), full saved r31 [F+336,F+344) and saved low32 LR [F+344,F+348). Full working r31=P and actual SP=F survive. The live leaf LR is the fill continuation 0x826A7C14; the wrapper's earlier return remains in its saved cell. This closes retention for this call only.
fill255Boundary.counterexample: An independent byte-address model checked four supplied aligned frames, including F=0xFFFFFE90, for exact set equality and save exclusion. Incorrectly retaining original count 255 for post-prefix tails produces 258 bytes and overwrites saved-r31 offsets F+336..F+338. An aligned-only fill theorem therefore cannot justify this unaligned call without the changed count.

copy256Boundary.question: Does the selected fixed-count 256-byte copy return normally while retaining the wrapper frame and adjacent saves?
copy256Boundary.call: 0x826A7C20 calls 0x827F4390 with full r3=D=F+80, r4=P=0xFFFFFFFF8208F5D8 and r5=256, returning to 0x826A7C24. Reuse fill255Boundary's admitted zero-extended, ABI-aligned, nonwrapping wrapper frame S=F+352 and retained full working r31=P.
copy256Boundary.predicates: Require retained executable/LR state, completing readable selected prefix at low32(P), writable mapped [D,D+256), stable source and no interfering writer. Require physically distinct destination bytes, no destructive physical alias with protected frame/caller/code/return state, and source/destination physical disjointness for claims about original source bytes. These are fixed-call premises, not observed mapping or activation facts.
copy256Boundary.copyAndPadding: If the first zero is at offset z in 0..255, byte load/store sites 0x827F439C/0x827F43A8 execute z+1 times, copying the zero, and r5=256-z. Site 0x827F43C4 sets r10=255-z. For z<255, 0x827F43D8 loads that positive full value into CTR and the 0x827F43DC byte store emits exactly 255-z further zeros; z=255 returns at 0x827F43C8 without a tail. If all first256 bytes are nonzero, the copy executes256 times, r5 becomes0 and 0x827F43C0 returns without another read or store. There is no forced terminator in that case.
copy256Boundary.finiteReturn: Under completing accesses, the fixed leaf returns through unchanged live LR in at most2053 instructions. For z<255 the count is783+5*z; z=255 and all256nonzero each take2053. Every admitted case performs exactly256 ordered distinct one-byte stores at D..D+255, with full final r11=D+256=F+336. There is no stack access, outgoing call, vector operation or explicit cache operation.
copy256Boundary.returnEffects: Let R=z+1 when a zero is found, otherwise R=256. Full r3 remains D and final full r4=P+R. Found-zero final r5=256-z and r10=255-z; all-nonzero final r5=0 and r10 is the last zero-extended source byte. r9 and CTR become0 only for z<255; otherwise their incoming values survive. Only GPR r4/r5/r9/r10/r11, CR0/CR6, XER.CA and conditionally CTR are assigned. Final XER.CA=1. CR0.GT=1 for z<255, otherwise CR0.EQ=1; CR6.GT=1 for a found zero, otherwise CR6.EQ=1, with LT=0, the other GT/EQ bit0 and SO from unchanged XER.SO. Full r1/SP, r31, all other GPRs, LR, other CR fields, XER except CA and floating/vector state remain unchanged.
copy256Boundary.saveRetention: Writes cover [F+80,F+336), excluding backchain [F,F+4), full saved r31 [F+336,F+344) and saved low32 LR [F+344,F+348). Actual SP=F and full working r31=P survive. The earlier fill's byte F+80 may now change. Live LR is the copy continuation0x826A7C24; the wrapper's earlier return remains in its saved cell. Retention depends on the stated physical-alias premises.
copy256Boundary.counterexamples: An independent all-nonzero256-byte Q witness leaves D+255=0x51, falsifying forced NUL termination. A supplied physical alias with unchanged full P but physical(P)=physical(D)-1 turns original A,0,B,... into256 A output bytes: writes destroy the unread zero. Original-prefix content/read-count claims therefore require source disjointness; no actual alias was established.
